findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and snapshots are stored unencrypted, exposing data if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, greatly expanding the attack surface for a database holding application data. The db_endpoint output further advertises this endpoint.

The master username is hard-coded to the predictable value 'admin' and the password is passed via a Terraform variable that is also interpolated into EC2 user data, making brute-force and credential-leak attacks easier. No IAM database authentication is enabled.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general/slowquery) are configured, so database access to a publicly reachable instance cannot be audited or investigated after compromise.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the RDS master username and plaintext password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance or via SSRF, leaking database credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; a web-server SSRF on the PHP application could retrieve instance profile credentials and the plaintext user data containing DB credentials.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is specified, so the instance volume containing the file with plaintext database credentials may be stored unencrypted.
The bootstrap script installs and serves the employee application over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS), transmitting user-submitted data in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web instance; compromise of the instance yields near-full control of S3 data, EC2, and RDS across the account, including privilege escalation paths.
The RDS security group allows all outbound traffic on all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting data exfiltration or C2 communication from the database tier with no network boundary.
The security group has no description and relies on rules defined elsewhere; combined with publicly_accessible RDS the group provides no documented, least-privilege boundary for the database tier.
